quizzes.stem: Scenario: Cobalt Logistics has three proposals for a returns-handling service. One has no way to learn from wrong answers, one is a workflow and one is a team of agents. A board member wants the cheapest. What should the architect do first?

options.a: Compare the prompts and model choice of each, since those decide the quality
options.b: Judge all of them on the same four stages and drop any that lacks one
options.c: Ask each team to run its design on a hundred real returns and compare the token bills
options.d: Choose the workflow because workflows cost less than an agent on this workload

explanation.b: A review applies the same questions to every design, and the missing stage is the first finding.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the missing feedback loop "is an architecture finding that no prompt can fix".
explanation.c: Ruled out because price is compared only "among those that pass the review".
explanation.d: Ruled out because choosing on price skips the review, and "a design with a missing stage or an unapproved write is rejected first".

quizzes.stem: Scenario: Heron Analytics' task splits into six independent parts, and one context could not hold all the reading, but its value is about the cost of a single chat. What should the architect conclude?

options.a: Build the team, since independence and volume together already justify its cost
options.b: Build the team with fewer subagents, so that its price falls below the task's value
options.c: Build neither, since even an agent alone would be priced above what the work earns
options.d: Build one agent, since the team is ruled out but a single agent still pays

explanation.c: Independence and volume hold but value fails: an agent costs about 4 chats and a team about 15, so neither pays and the question becomes "whether the task is worth automating at all".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "a team that fails the third loses money on every run".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "The answer is not a cheaper team."
explanation.d: Ruled out because for this task "its value is below what even one agent costs".

quizzes.stem: Scenario: At Alder Freight an intake service and a pricing service each pass every one of their own tests. In production about one request in fifty stalls between them, and always for shipments with no matching tariff. What does this most likely indicate?

options.a: A pricing model too weak to cope with the unusual shipments it receives
options.b: An unwritten rule for how the two parts treat a lookup that finds nothing
options.c: A transient network fault that an automatic retry would clear on the next attempt
options.d: A defect inside the intake service that its own tests have never covered

explanation.b: Both parts pass their own checks, so the gap is what neither contract says about the empty case.
explanation.a: Ruled out because a bigger model "only changes how the same ambiguity is worded".
explanation.c: Ruled out because a failure that follows an input pattern "is deterministic, and a retry repeats it".
explanation.d: Ruled out because each service passes its own tests, and of such a pair the page says "Neither is wrong by its own rules."

quizzes.stem: Scenario: Cobalt Freight's design has an input stage, a processing stage, a feedback loop and an output stage that writes the model's text straight into the shipping database with no check. What does the rubric report?

options.a: No finding, since all four stages are present in the design and the loop is in place
options.b: A high finding, so the verdict is reject whatever the price of the whole design
options.c: A medium finding, so the verdict is revise until a vetting step is added
options.d: A missing-stage finding for output, since an unchecked stage does not count

explanation.c: A stage that exists but lets text through unchecked is a medium finding, and a medium finding gives `revise`.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the rubric raises a finding when "There is an output stage that has no validation step".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "any `high` gives `reject`, otherwise any `medium` gives `revise`", and nothing here is high.
explanation.d: Ruled out because a missing-stage finding is raised when "A stage is empty or absent", and this output stage exists and writes to the database.

quizzes.stem: Scenario: Fenwick Bank's design review turns up two problems, one rated medium and one rated high. What outcome does the rubric give?

options.a: Revise, because the medium problem is the one that can be repaired most easily
options.b: Reject, since the more severe of the two findings decides the whole verdict
options.c: Revise, leaving the price to decide whether it beats the other designs
options.d: Revise, because the two ratings are averaged into one level of severity

explanation.b: The verdict follows the worst finding, and a `high` gives `reject`.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "any `high` gives `reject`, otherwise any `medium` gives `revise`".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Price enters last, and only among the designs that were not rejected".
explanation.d: Ruled out because there is no averaging: "The verdict follows the worst finding".

quizzes.stem: Scenario: Willow Bank's complaint triage design collects a rating from customers for every reply and stores the ratings in a table that nobody reads. How should the review treat the feedback stage?

options.a: As present, since a rating is collected for every reply that customers receive
options.b: As absent, since nothing in the system ever changes because of those scores
options.c: As absent, which the rubric rates as medium, so the verdict is revise
options.d: As present, since the ratings stay available for anyone who later wants them

explanation.b: The stage is defined by "the path by which they change the system", and here there is none.
explanation.a: Ruled out because collecting a rating is logging and not a loop: the stage holds "Evaluation, logging, human corrections, and the path by which they change the system".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the rubric lists `no-feedback` as high, and "any `high` gives `reject`".
explanation.d: Ruled out because ratings that sit unread are not a loop, and a pipeline that "never learns from the result, goes wrong silently and stays wrong".

quizzes.stem: Scenario: Quince Retail runs a returns agent that writes refunds to the ledger without approval, and the auditors require a record of each approval. What does the rubric report?

options.a: A medium finding, so the verdict is revise until an approval step is added
options.b: No finding, since the agent's answers have already been validated before the write
options.c: An autonomy finding, since the agent acts with no person in the loop
options.d: A high finding, which makes the verdict reject whatever the cost of the design

explanation.d: A write without approval where an audit is needed is a `high` finding, so the verdict is reject.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "The verdict follows the worst finding", and the rubric names `high` for this one.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the rule fires when "The design writes without approval and an audit is needed", whatever was validated.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the autonomy finding is about need, not oversight, and applies only when "An agent or a team is used on a path that is already known".
